newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Swiss journalist expelled from Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Swiss journalist expelled from Zaire.

text.p: A Swiss journalist was expelled from Zaire on Sunday by the authorities after writing articles speaking of the demoralised state of the Zairean army.
Jean-Philippe Ceppi, who was sent to Zaire by French daily Liberation, was held in the Shaba Province capital Lubumbashi on Thursday, and escorted on a plane to Kinshasa the next day.
"They said I had not respected the proper protocol, and acccused me of telling lies," Ceppi told Reuters just before leaving Kinshasa for Johannesburg.
"They said that a report I broadcast on BBC had spread panic in Kinshasa, and that people here were saying that the province (Shaba) is no longer defended," he said.
Rebels who took up arms in eastern Zaire last October took their war into mineral-producing Shaba Province by the end of January despite a government counter-offensive launched earlier.
Ceppi had no complaints about the way he had been treated during almost two days of detention and questioning.
The offending report broadcast on the BBC World Service radio in French described a train allegedly hijacked by soldiers fleeing rebel advances in the copper-rich province.
Ceppi reported 13 soldiers forced the driver of what he called the "mad train" to stop in villages along the railway while they looted and loaded the train with their booty.
He said more disciplined troops arrested the soldiers on Wednesday.
Ceppi said authorities in Kinshasa had asked him to leave, and come back at a later less sensitive time.
He is the third international journalist ordered from sensitive areas near the war zone in eastern Zaire.
Ten days ago two French journalists, from Radio France Internationale and Le Monde newspaper, were asked to leave the city of Kisangani where the Zairean army headquarters is based.
